chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, Ibn Bukayr, and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'What do you say regarding marrying the people, for I have reached the age you see and have never married.' He said, 'And what prevents you from that?' I said, 'Nothing prevents me except that I fear that marrying them may not be permissible for me. So what do you order me?' He said, 'How do you deal with it while you are young? Do you remain patient?' I said, 'I take the slave girls.'

He said, 'Tell me now, so how do you make the slave girls permissible? Inform me.' I said, 'The slave girl is not at the status of the free woman. If the slave girl causes me doubt about something, I sell her or keep away from her.' He said, 'Explain to me, so how do you make her permissible?' He said, 'So there was no answer with me.'
I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Inform me, what is your view, shall I get married?' He said, 'What do I care if you were to do it.' I said, 'Can you see your words,

He said, 'Surely, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had married, and there was from the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has related, and Allah the Exalted has said: Allah sets forth an example to those who disbelieve - the wife of Nuh and the wife of Lut: they were both under two of Our righteous servants, but they acted treacherously towards them.'

So I said, 'Surely, as for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), I am not of a status like that. But rather, she was in his hands and she agreed with his ruling, manifesting his religion. But, by Allah, I do not mean by that except with regards to the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:

I said, 'May Allah keep you well! So what do you order me for? Shall I go and get married by your order?' So he said, 'If you were to do so, upon you is with the simple ones from the women.' I said, 'And what is the simple one?' He said, 'The veiled one, the chaste.' So I said, 'The one who is upon the religion of Salim Abu Hafs?' So he said, 'No.' I said, 'The one who is upon the religion of Rabi'ah al-Ra'i?' He said, 'No, but the young ones who are not hostile (Nasibi) and are not understanding what you are understanding (Wilayah).'

key_terms.لَا يَعْرِفْنَ مَا تَعْرِفُونَ: Not understanding what you understand (regarding Wilayah)

ai.seo_question: What type of women did the Imam recommend for marriage to avoid religious complications?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses a companion's hesitation to marry free women due to fears of religious incompatibility, particularly with the 'Nasibi' (hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt). He advises marrying slave girls who are 'balha''—characterized by simplicity, modesty, and a lack of deep knowledge regarding Wilayah—to minimize the risk of religious deviation affecting the household. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical marital compatibility and the preservation of faith through selecting spouses with suitable, albeit less complex, religious dispositions.
